title: 3 Cryptocurrencies That Will Benefit From a Rate Cut | The Motley Fool
content: The Motley Fool article argues that Bitcoin, Dogecoin, and XRP could rise as the Federal Reserve cuts rates in 2025. It cites that the Fed has cut its benchmark rate three times in 2024 and that analysts expect at least one or two more cuts as inflation cools. Bitcoin, with a 21‑million‑token cap and 19.9 million already mined, has benefited from spot‑ETF approvals, its April 2024 halving, and regulatory easing, positioning it as a digital‑gold hedge that may strengthen when the U.S. dollar weakens. Dogecoin, an inflationary PoW token with nearly 150 billion coins in circulation, is buoyed by celebrity endorsements (Elon Musk’s 2021 Tesla acceptance and his brief involvement with the Department of Government Efficiency), a large social‑media following (2.7 million subreddit members and 11.2 billion TikTok views), and potential ETF approvals and the expansion of Dogechain on Polygon. XRP, pre‑mined at 100 billion tokens, has recovered after the SEC lawsuit, and its growth is supported by a spot‑ETF launch, increasing use as a bridge currency for cross‑border payments, and a developing developer ecosystem using lightweight ‘hooks’. The article suggests these catalysts could lift the three tokens above Bitcoin and other established cryptocurrencies as the market heats up again.

title: Surprise: DOGE didn't actually cut spending.
content: Elon Musk announced during a public appearance in Washington, D.C., riding a Cybertruck, that he would cut up to $2 trillion in government spending. However, according to the Congressional Budget Office (CBO), federal spending actually increased by $220 billion—4% higher than the previous year. Spending rose across nearly all major categories, with only two exceptions: the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), which saw reduced spending due to fewer bank failures, and the Small Business Administration (SBA), whose disaster-related loan costs did not recur in 2025 as they had in 2024. The CBO report confirms that the anticipated spending cuts did not materialize.

title: DOGE Budget Black Hole Shocks Washington: DOT Miners Operate Steadily Amid Volatility, Users Earn Up to $8,600 Daily
content: The article reports that the use of Dogecoin (DOGE) by Elon Musk's 'Government Efficiency Unit' to claim $1 trillion in federal budget cuts has sparked controversy in Washington, with no verified savings or transparent funding destinations confirmed by Congress. This 'fiscal black box' has shaken confidence in U.S. fiscal transparency and prompted scrutiny of how decentralized crypto systems may be reshaping global capital flows. Despite macroeconomic volatility, DOT Miners' cloud mining platform has maintained stability, with users earning an average of $8,600 daily during a high-volatility period. According to Aaron Choi, chief analyst at DOT Miners, the DOGE initiative represents an 'institutional experiment in crypto' that demonstrates the resilience of distributed computing systems when centralized finances falter. The platform offers flexible mining plans with daily returns ranging from $3.50 to $5,300, depending on investment size, with full principal returned at contract end. Key features include regulatory compliance (UK-based), 100% renewable energy usage, Bitmain technical backing, multi-layered security, and a referral bonus program offering 4.5% lifetime commission. DOT Miners plans global expansion into North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, with future developments including AI-driven income optimization and compliant cross-chain financial products to support a sustainable crypto-finance ecosystem.

title: " Où est passé l'argent ? " Un mystère entoure les milliards d'économies revendiquées par le DOGE d'Elon Musk
content: Elon Musk's 'Department of Government Efficiency' (DOGE), launched under President Donald Trump, promised to save $1 trillion in federal spending by September 30, 2024, but has failed to deliver on this pledge. Despite the fiscal year closing, the actual savings remain unclear due to inconsistent accounting, obscured reporting by the White House, and the lack of transparency in how funds were used. Independent budget experts, members of Congress, and the public have no clear picture of where the money went. The Congressional Budget Office and other oversight bodies have been unable to verify DOGE's claimed $214 billion in savings, which were inflated through double-counting contracts, underestimating litigation costs, and misrepresenting cancellations. The DOGE, created by executive decree, lacked legal authority to reduce spending—only Congress can cancel funds via 'rescission' legislation. During the fiscal year, only two rescission requests were submitted, totaling $14 billion, far below DOGE's claims. Analysts estimate actual cuts may be around $16 billion, while Democrats cite up to $410 billion in frozen or canceled spending. The Office of Management and Budget (OMB), led by Russell Vought, played a key role in blocking disbursements and suppressing public data, violating a 1974 law that prohibits freezing funds allocated by Congress. Vought has declared the law unconstitutional and plans to challenge it in court. The controversy has sparked a constitutional crisis over separation of powers, with Democrats accusing the administration of undermining Congress's fiscal authority. Experts from both sides agree that the real impact of DOGE was not fiscal savings but the expansion of executive power, as the administration used the initiative to bypass legislative oversight and increase control over federal spending. The confusion and deliberate obfuscation have persisted beyond Musk’s initial public interest, enabling a long-term shift in power toward the executive branch.

title: Elon Musk anuncia que abandona su rol como asesor del gobierno de Trump tras criticar el proyecto presupuestario de los republicanos
content: Elon Musk announced on October 11, 2025, that he is ending his role as a special government employee in Donald Trump's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), concluding his 130-day annual tenure starting January 20, 2025. Musk, appointed by Trump as the 'savings czar,' had led efforts to reduce government spending, including eliminating foreign aid funds. In a post on X, Musk thanked Trump and expressed confidence that DOGE would become a lasting 'way of life' across government. However, his departure follows public criticism of Trump's congressional budget proposal, which includes $600 billion in projected deficit increases, tax extensions, defense spending hikes, and a debt ceiling rise to $4 trillion. Musk stated he was 'disappointed' with the plan, claiming it 'undermines' DOGE’s work and fails to reduce spending. The budget, described by Trump as 'great and beautiful,' is now under Senate review. Musk's criticism marks a growing rift with Trump, despite Musk's $250 million in donations that helped secure Trump’s 2024 election victory. DOGE previously claimed $175 billion in savings, though the BBC found this figure unsupported. Musk also announced plans to reduce his political involvement and commit to leading Tesla for five more years, despite ongoing backlash, boycotts, and declining sales tied to his DOGE role. He defended his actions, saying, 'I did what had to be done.'

title: 'Not even close': Conservative WSJ hammers Elon Musk's DOGE over cost-cutting flop
content: The Wall Street Journal reports that the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), led by Elon Musk, failed to deliver on its promise of $2 trillion in federal spending reductions. Despite Musk's January 2025 claims of a comprehensive plan to achieve massive savings, actual spending rose by $220 billion, or 4%, for the fiscal year. Excluding a $131 billion non-cash write-off by the Donald Trump administration, non-interest spending increased by $351 billion, and total spending rose by $55 billion in September 2025 compared to the prior year. The Journal stated the results were 'Not even close' to the promised savings. DOGE did recover some grants and terminate probationary employees, with minor savings expected in fiscal 2026 when deferred resignations take effect. However, these measures have not significantly altered the overall spending trend. Additionally, hundreds of workers previously laid off by DOGE have been asked to return to work after months of paid time off.

title: DOGE Says $5.8 Billion Saved From 100 Terminated Federal Contracts
content: The Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), established by President Donald Trump on his first day in office, announced the termination of 108 federal contracts with a combined ceiling value of $5.8 billion, resulting in $397 million in savings, according to an October 10 post on X. Among the terminated contracts were a $3.1 million State Department project for the 'Tanzania National Coordination Office Development,' a $46,500 U.S. Agency for Global Media lease for Voice of America East Asia and Pacific Service office space, a $5.8 million HHS contract for leadership training, and a $44 million State Department contract for professional services in Doha, Qatar. Since its inception, DOGE has reported approximately $214 billion in estimated savings, or about $1,329.19 per taxpayer, as of October 4. The agency has also posted 13,440 contract terminations ($61 billion), 15,887 grant terminations ($49 billion), and 264 lease terminations ($113 million) on its website. DOGE was created by reorganizing the former U.S. Digital Service and granted full access to unclassified agency records, software, and IT systems. President Trump issued orders in January and February directing agencies to review and terminate or modify contracts and grants to reduce spending and eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse. Elon Musk, a former special government employee and adviser, led DOGE until his departure in late May. The administration has also seen over 201,000 federal employees leave by September 23, with some offered 'deferred resignation' packages. Ongoing reductions-in-force are occurring amid a government shutdown that began on October 1, with around 4,100 workers receiving layoff notices. A memo from the Office of Management and Budget stated that programs with funding lapses during the shutdown are no longer statutorily required to operate, and agencies must submit reduction-in-force plans for review.

title: Musk Promised To Cut $2 Trillion. Government Spending Went Up Instead
content: According to the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) fiscal year 2025 report, federal spending excluding interest rose by $220 billion, or 4%, despite Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) claiming to cut $2 trillion, then $1 trillion, and finally $150 billion in savings. The actual spending increase was even more severe—$351 billion—when excluding a $131 billion noncash adjustment related to student loan program modifications, which were not real savings. DOGE's only measurable spending reductions came from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (fewer bank failures) and the Small Business Administration (no repeat of 2024 disaster loan costs), neither tied to DOGE's efforts. Meanwhile, Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid—accounting for the largest spending increases—rose by 8% due to demographic and healthcare cost trends, not bureaucratic inefficiency. DOGE’s actions led to the destruction of essential programs like USAID, which had prevented 92 million deaths between 2001 and 2021, based on Musk’s conspiracy theories. The agency’s mass firings caused operational breakdowns, prompting widespread rehiring across agencies such as the GSA, IRS, Labor Department, and National Park Service, at higher costs due to the chaos. The CBO data confirms that DOGE was not a fiscal efficiency initiative but an ideological campaign that increased government spending, damaged public services, and cost taxpayers more than it saved. The failure was predictable, as DOGE treated complex governance like a tech startup to be 'disrupted,' ignoring the expertise required to maintain essential functions. The final outcome: a $21.7 billion waste in six months and a legacy of expensive chaos that undermines democratic governance.

title: DOGE loses some steam without Elon Musk
content: Elon Musk departed DOGE in late May after a turbulent tenure that included lawsuits, clashes with law‑enforcement, and questions over alleged fraud. Senior aide Katie Miller and eight other core staffers also left. 19‑year‑old Edward Coristine, known as 'Big Balls', was physically attacked near Dupont Circle in early August and is now with the Social Security Administration. U.S. District Court Judge Tanya Chutkan refused to dismiss a lawsuit from 14 Democratic state attorneys general that alleged DOGE’s actions were illegal, though she removed Trump from the suit. A GSA spokesperson told the Washington Examiner that DOGE continues to root out waste, claiming it has saved roughly $206 billion—far below Musk’s original $2 trillion goal. The GSA is asking hundreds of DOGE‑laid‑off employees to decide by week’s end whether to return; if they accept, they must resume work on Oct. 6 after a seven‑month paid vacation. The GSA’s Public Buildings Service is reorganizing from a geographic to a program‑based model, with 11 regions replaced by national business units. Other agencies—FDA, IRS, HUD, USDA, Labor, National Park Service, and NNSA—have also asked former DOGE workers to return. GOP strategist Dennis Lennox said the "whole approach of storming the offices… and then basically trying to unilaterally disband an entity… was never going to work." An anonymous Republican noted that DOGE still has "teeth" because Congress has enacted rescission packages. Former DOGE co‑head Vivek Ramaswamy said he and Musk disagreed on priorities, citing an over‑grown regulatory state and national debt. In mid‑July the House approved a $9 billion rescission package that clawed back $1.1 billion for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting and roughly $7 billion in foreign aid, which Trump signed into law. The Republican source said the hardest thing in the federal government is pulling back a program once it’s started, and that "people on Capitol Hill don’t have the will to bring spending in line."

title: DOGE Savings Top $200 Billion, Almost $1,300 Per Taxpayer
content: The Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) has terminated 123 'wasteful contracts' worth $5.3 billion, resulting in savings of $4.2 billion. The canceled contracts included a $1.5 million Treasury Department contract for 'Word Processing and Document Formatting Services Examination Training' and a $785,000 State Department consulting contract for staffing. DOGE dismissed media reports that its cost savings methodology is faulty, saying 'in federal contracting, ceilings matter because they are almost always maxed out.' As of August 15, DOGE had saved an estimated $205 billion for the federal government, amounting to $1,273.29 saved per U.S. taxpayer. However, a group of Democratic senators introduced the Pick Up After Your DOGE Act, which calls for a comprehensive audit of computer systems and networks of federal agencies accessed by DOGE staff, citing 'substantial risks' to sensitive data and the well-being of Americans.
